node-1.label: Progressively worsening dyspnea and diarrhea of 1 week's duration

node-2.label: A man in his 60s with a history of end-stage renal disease status post renal transplant, atrial fibrillation, and sick sinus syndrome status after dual-chamber pacemaker placement

node-3.label: Patient denied chest pain, palpitations, or syncope

node-4.label: Physical examination: hypoxia requiring 4 L/min oxygen, blood pressure 130/79 mm Hg, heart rate 90 bpm, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral pulmonary basilar crackles, and lower extremity pitting edema

node-5.label: Acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload

why.why: Echocardiography shows LVEF 35% and chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, directly confirming systolic heart failure with pulmonary edema. Combined with elevated JVP, bilateral crackles, lower extremity edema, and hypoxia, acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload is established. Normal wall motion and denied chest pain/palpitations/syncope support a non-ischemic cause. Confidence increased from 0.75 to 0.95.

Expert analyses from the Laboratory Physician and Radiologist both confirm that the combination of LVEF 35%, severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, elevated JVP, crackles, edema, and hypoxia establishes acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload. The imaging and exam pattern is characteristic of cardiac volume overload rather than infection, and no infectious focus has been identified. Diarrhea remains nonspecific, so infection in this immunocompromised host is further downgraded from 0.1 to 0.05.

node-7.label: Renal allograft dysfunction causing fluid overload

why.why: Echocardiography showing LVEF 35% with normal wall motion localizes the fluid overload to cardiac systolic dysfunction rather than primary renal allograft failure. Expert analyses confirm that the severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, elevated JVP, crackles, edema, and hypoxia are fully explained by acute decompensated heart failure. Renal dysfunction may coexist but is not the primary driver, so confidence is lowered from 0.1 to 0.05.

node-8.label: Echocardiography shows left ventricular ejection fraction of 35%

node-10.label: Chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion

node-11.label: Patient has systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)

why.why: Echocardiography demonstrates LVEF 35% and chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, establishing systolic dysfunction with pulmonary edema. Laboratory and Radiology expert analyses independently confirm that these imaging and physical examination findings are sufficient to diagnose HFrEF, and the still-pending BNP result is not essential. The absence of chest pain, palpitations, or syncope and normal wall motion further support a non-ischemic mechanism. Confidence is raised from 0.9 to 0.95.

node-12.label: Patient has non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction

attrs.why: The patient denied chest pain, palpitations, or syncope, and echocardiography shows normal wall motion despite LVEF 35%. Laboratory and Radiology expert analyses interpret these features as favoring a non-ischemic mechanism. This supports non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction as the underlying etiology of the HFrEF. Confidence is 0.7 because coronary ischemia cannot be completely excluded without further evaluation.
